title: Alibaba Drops Gaming Arm as AI Takes Center Stage
excerpt: Alibaba sells its gaming arm, Lingxi Games, to Trustar Capital in a reported $1.5 billion deal, days before earnings.
content_html:
Alibaba Group Holding (BABA) is selling its gaming unit, Lingxi Games, to Asian private equity firm Trustar Capital in a transaction reportedly worth at least $1.5 billion.

The sale comes as CEO Eddie Wu makes artificial intelligence and cloud computing key strategic priorities for the company.

Why Alibaba Is Letting Go of Gaming

Lingxi CEO Zhou Bingshu told employees in a Monday memo that the handover frees Alibaba to concentrate on its strategic priorities.

"Alibaba is handing Lingxi to Trustar due to better focus on its strategic priorities," Zhou said.

Chief executive Eddie Wu has been pruning assets outside the company's core. Alibaba sold its controlling stake in hypermarket operator Sun Art Retail Group to DCP Capital for roughly $1.6 billion in January 2025.

Trustar Capital, an Asian buyout firm, emerged as the preferred bidder ahead of strategic buyers from the gaming industry, people familiar with the matter said. The reported price tops the roughly 9 billion yuan Alibaba was earlier expected to fetch.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

The $100 Billion AI Target Behind the Sale

In March, Alibaba outlined its goal to pass $100 billion in combined AI and cloud revenue within five years. The company has already pledged 380 billion yuan, about $53 billion, to that infrastructure over three years.

Momentum has followed. Alibaba shipped its largest model to date this month. Arena ranked Qwen3.8-Max fourth on its frontend coding leaderboard, behind two Claude Opus 5 variants and Moonshot's Kimi K3.

That push sits inside a wider contest with US labs. Chinese AI model usage has already surpassed that of American rivals in monthly tokens processed.

Alibaba reports June quarter results on Thursday, August 20. The number that matters is whether AI-related product revenue continues to compound fast enough to justify the divestments that fund the shift.

content_html_zh:
阿里巴巴集团控股公司 (BABA) 正在将其游戏部门灵犀游戏出售给亚洲私募股权公司 Trustar Capital，据报道，这笔交易价值至少 15 亿美元。

此次出售正值首席执行官吴艾迪将人工智能和云计算列为公司的关键战略重点之际。

阿里巴巴为何放弃游戏

灵犀首席执行官周秉树在周一的一份备忘录中告诉员工，此次交接让阿里巴巴得以腾出时间专注于其战略重点。

“阿里巴巴将灵犀交给 Trustar 是为了更好地专注于其战略重点，”周说。

首席执行官吴艾迪一直在削减公司核心以外的资产。 2025 年 1 月，阿里巴巴以约 16 亿美元的价格将其大卖场运营商高鑫零售集团的控股权出售给德汇资本。

知情人士称，亚洲收购公司 Trustar Capital 成为优先竞标者，领先于游戏行业的战略买家。 报道的价格高于阿里巴巴此前预计的约 90 亿元人民币的价格。

在 X 上关注我们以获取最新消息

此次出售背后的 1000 亿美元人工智能目标

今年 3 月，阿里巴巴制定了五年内人工智能和云收入合计突破 1000 亿美元的目标。 该公司已承诺在三年内为该基础设施投资 3800 亿元人民币（约合 530 亿美元）。

势头随之而来。 阿里巴巴本月发货了迄今为止最大的型号。 Arena 将 Qwen3.8-Max 在其前端编码排行榜上排名第四，落后于两个 Claude Opus 5 变体和 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3。

这一推动是与美国实验室进行更广泛的竞争的一部分。 在每月处理的代币数量上，中国人工智能模型的使用率已经超过了美国竞争对手。

阿里巴巴将于 8 月 20 日星期四公布 6 月份季度业绩。 重要的数字是人工智能相关产品的收入是否继续以足够快的速度复合，以证明为这一转变提供资金的撤资是合理的。
